facts.statement: A new species named Triodus richterae was described in 2017 from fossils found in the Rio do Rasto Formation in Brazil.
facts.quote: In 2017, a new species Triodus richterae was described from the Rio do Rasto Formation of Brazil.

facts.statement: Triodus was an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish that lived during the Carboniferous and Permian periods.
facts.quote: Triodus is an extinct genus of xenacanthiform cartilaginous fish that lived from the Carboniferous to the Permian.

facts.statement: The genus Triodus was first described by Jordan in 1849.
Triodus belongs to the extinct family Xenacanthidae.
Triodus was an extinct genus of elasmobranchs in the order Xenacanthiformes that lived from the Carboniferous to the Triassic periods.
facts.quote: Triodus es un género extinto de elasmobranquios del orden Xenacanthiformes que vivieron entre los periodos Carbonífero al Triásico.

facts.statement: Fossils of Triodus have been found in the Chinle Formation and Black Prince Limestone of Arizona, the Petrified Forest Member of New Mexico, and the Tecovas Formation of Texas in the United States.
facts.quote: sus fósiles han sido hallados en la Formación Chinle y la Caliza Black Prince de Arizona, el Miembro Bosque Petrificado de Nuevo México y la Formación Tecovas de Texas, en Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: The time range for Triodus extends from the Bashkirian to the Norian stages, between 323.4 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bashkirian to Norian (323.4 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group for the genus Triodus is the family Xenacanthidae.
